Code simplification requires a reproducible behavior snapshot and equivalent before/after evidence plus focused checks (code-simplification 22-34). Documentation work limits verification to links and safe commands when authorized and labels unavailable checks (documentation-and-adrs 39-42). The shared engineering manual calls for deterministic behavior-focused tests at changed boundaries, exact evidence, and measurement-led optimization (shared/references/engineering-principles.md 43-55). The inspected workflows specify distinct assurance needs; no redundant check sequence was evident from their instructions alone.

Performance optimization explicitly requires metric, representative workload, environment, sample method, threshold, correctness oracle, and a reproducible baseline; it stops without a valid baseline (performance-optimization 22-29), compares equivalent conditions and requires reporting variance and rollback conditions (30-38). Engineering principles independently state that optimization must be based on measurements and a performance target (shared/references/engineering-principles.md 48-50). No additional measurement mechanism or confirmed gap was found in the scoped sources.

The three assigned skills do not include skill-local copies of the engineering manual or reference it as a prerequisite; their distinct tasks own separate evidence/verification policies. The inspected root manual supplies general cross-cutting principles. Project instructions state that the manual is authoritative under root shared/ and that generated skill-local copies exist for self-contained global installations (protocol.md lines 13-17; project AGENTS.md supplied in active context). This is an intentional distribution boundary, not enough evidence for a deduplication recommendation.
